messages:
rachel_sales: NovaHealth POC question: they want Redwood Private deployed into their transit VPC, must retain original client IP for auditing, and they do TLS inspection in their DMZ. Also asked: cost delta between allocating static EIPs per AZ vs using a shared NAT gateway. Need a short checklist and plain-language answer for customer.

devin_se: Short answer: yes we can do Private deploy with interface endpoints. Preserving client IP depends on where SNAT occurs. If traffic goes through a centralized TGW NAT you'll generally see the NAT IP. Options: NLB+EIP, PROXY protocol/X-Forwarded-For from their proxy, or 1:1 SNAT.

aj_netops: Quick question: how will on-prem connect to cloud? The topology changes recommendations: PrivateLink (interface endpoints) terminates at ENIs and preserves client IP if you avoid SNAT; TGW/spoke with central NAT will SNAT. VPN/Direct Connect with TGW often hairpins.

rachel_sales: They plan Direct Connect into a transit TGW for low jitter, but ops also wants PrivateLink for service endpoints. Security team requires a firewall allowlist and clarity on whether TLS-inspect breaks mTLS.

priya_sec: Security note: TLS inspection in customer DMZ is fine but they must keep certificate ownership and private keys. We recommend terminating mutual TLS at the connector inside their VPC (Redwood side supports mTLS). We do not recommend the customer perform MITM on our control-plane certs. I'll draft the exact wording for the security questionnaire (TLS versions, ciphers, mTLS flow, KMS integration, audit log retention).

devin_se: Pasteable firewall snippet they can use (recommend FQDN allowlist where possible):

```
# Customer outbound egress (to Redwood Private endpoints)
Outbound allow: TCP 443 -> *.redwood-private.<region>.svc
Outbound allow: UDP 123 -> 0.0.0.0/0  # NTP
Outbound allow: TCP 54321 -> <optional health probe IPs>

# If they require inbound health checks
Inbound allow: TCP 443 <- <redwood-healthcheck-ips>
```

We also publish a JSON of IP ranges in onboarding; FQDN is preferred to avoid churn.

aj_netops: Practical approaches to retain client src IP: 
- NLB (internal) fronting our service + static EIP on NLB -> upstream sees EIP but we can map to customer.
- Proxy in DMZ that forwards PROXY protocol or X-Forwarded-For to the backend (app must understand it).
- Per-host 1:1 SNATs / EIP allocation (costly but preserves mapping).
Note: ALB will not preserve source IP without proxy protocol. If TGW NAT sits in path you'll get NAT IP.

rachel_sales: Pricing ask from NovaHealth: "what's the incremental monthly cost for per-AZ static eips vs NAT gateway?" Any ballpark to give them?

devin_se: High-level pricing guidance (ballpark):
- Per-static EIP mapping (managed by us) typically billed as a monthly per-EIP fee + standard egress. Expect a per-EIP SMP of ~$40-120/mo depending on region and contract (we'll confirm with finance).
- Shared NAT (using a single NAT gateway) is cheaper infra-wise but has no sticky customer-level source IP guarantees; NAT gateway costs are primarily cloud provider charges (hourly + data transfer).
I'll escalate to finance for exact numbers and attach to the onboarding doc. Flag: pricing varies by committed contract and Dedicated vs Private deployment.

ops-bot: [ops-bot] Onboarding checklist updated: https://redwood.internal/onboard/novahealth/connectivity (internal link)

aj_netops: Ops tips: watch MTU when you have IPsec/encapsulation — recommend PMTU ~1400 for streaming. Also call out TCP idle timeouts (keepalive <60s) for long lived streams. SNI preservation: if their TLS inspect rewrites SNI we need to coordinate TLS routing.

priya_sec: Security questionnaire items I'm adding: minimum TLS1.2 (prefer TLS1.3), allowed cipher suites, mTLS flow diagram, whether we accept customer CA bundle, KMS/HSM support, and audit log retention (30/90/365 options). I'll upload the text template.

devin_se: Action items: 
- Devin: create a 1-page decision matrix (PrivateLink vs TGW vs Peering) including src-IP tradeoffs, ALB/NLB notes, and PROXY header examples.
- AJ: write short ops note on DMZ proxy config, PROXY protocol example and MTU/keepalive settings.
- Priya: complete security questionnaire language (mTLS/KMS/audit).
- Rachel: collect NovaHealth's preference and whether they can accept PROXY headers or need EIP-per-AZ. Loop in finance for pricing.

rachel_sales: I'll run this by NovaHealth tomorrow and share the one-pager after your updates. Please drop artifacts in the onboarding link.

aj_netops: Also call out POC risk: multi-region failover + sticky egress is non-trivial; if they need global failover we should document expected behavior.

devin_se: Will have the matrix + diagram by EOD and include a sample security-friendly blurb for the customer.

rachel_sales: Thanks all :thumbsup: — this should keep the sales cycle moving.
